description: Motivated by reconnaissance visits after the January 2020 earthquake series in Puerto Rico, this paper discusses how damage from Hurricane Maria in 2017 may have interacted with the earthquakes, and what that means for future field reconnaissance, which usually focuses on one hazard. Case studies cover port facilities, buildings (particularly historic structures) and bridges, showing how hurricane impacts combined with ageing infrastructure and delayed repair and recovery may have shaped damage levels and failure modes. Coverage: surveyed sites in Puerto Rico. Access: open-access article in Frontiers in Built Environment (2023); the survey instrument is provided and the full reconnaissance data are published on NHERI DesignSafe. Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: attributing earthquake damage to earlier hurricane effects is inferred from observation, not measured before and after. Outcome: a case for documenting multi-hazard interactions and cascading effects in post-disaster assessments. Simulation uses: state-dependent fragility of damaged or unrepaired structures and sequential-hazard recovery modelling. Related records: DesignSafe Data Depot, StEER reconnaissance and the Puerto Rico informal reconstruction study.
